calls.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production orthographic creature turnaround for a UE game, M-09 Hanging Bell / 悬钟.
Input image 1 is the user supplied definitive creature identity reference, NOT a layout to reproduce. Redraw this exact creature into a clean, highly detailed, consistent FRONT / LEFT SIDE / BACK orthographic model reference sheet.
Create one wide landscape image, preferably 3072 x 2048. Three evenly spaced full-body views, all the same scale, same neutral hanging pose, exact horizontal alignment at fingertips, shoulders, abdomen and eye-crown tip. Plain very light warm-gray background, soft neutral studio illumination, almost no ground shadow, sharp silhouette, no perspective foreshortening. No scenery, beam, floor, chains to ceiling, people, measurements, captions over anatomy, detail inserts or additional views. Only tiny headings FRONT, LEFT SIDE, BACK above respective panels.
Identity: a suspended, legless laboratory organic horror. Exactly two enormous elongated muscular upper arms sweep out then curve upward over its narrow vertically stretched torso. Both big hands hook their five extremely long fingers inward around an absent support at identical height; pale worn numbered wrist restraint cuffs remain attached. No normal head at the shoulders. Two dark metal tissue anchor rings near upper back/shoulders. Exactly two smaller humanlike arms emerge on the FRONT lower torso, forearms loosely crossed in front just above the pendant eye-crown; their fingers must be individually readable. The heavy downward tapered oval eye-crown at the bottom of the trunk is made of folded pale tissue with embedded open gray-blue eyes of different sizes, largest eyes on the front/lateral surfaces; backside has a few smaller eyes. No feet, no legs, no mouth, no extra limbs.
Tissue design: three continuous overlapping leaf-like membrane lobes on EACH side, six total, attached along the posterior shoulder-to-upper-back tissue root band and draping down the sides like a layered biological bell mantle. The three lobes per side have clear distinct continuous shapes with scalloped ragged edges and a few organic fenestrations; do not shred them into floating strips. Outer upper lobe short, middle lobe intermediate, inner lower lobe long. All six are the same organ pieces in all views. At rest they mostly close around the torso with clear front clearance for the two small arms and eye-crown. Blue-gray vascular branching through pearly translucent-looking skin, fleshy structural veins and edge thickness. These are fleshy gill membranes, NOT feathered or bat wings; no added skeletal wing fingers. No flight pose.
Material fidelity to reference: pale gray ivory wet skin, slightly mauve tissue, subtle blue vascular membrane veins, weathered iron/ivory cuffs and metal rings, gray-blue irises. Restrained satin highlights reveal sculptural anatomy and membrane thickness, no exaggerated slime or gore.
View consistency: FRONT faces viewer and displays the small crossed arms; LEFT SIDE faces left in profile showing the small arms projecting toward the left and layered membranes behind toward the right; BACK shows spine and rear membrane roots and conceals the small front arms behind torso, never paste the crossed arms onto the back. The same body length of about 2.8m fingertip to eye-crown tip in all panels. Preserve the user's unusual suspended silhouette and details while simplifying the presentation into a usable modeling reference. Occluded back anatomy is a conservative production design reconstruction.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: anatomy separation and assembly design board for M-09 Hanging Bell, a fictional game creature. Image 1 is the original identity reference; image 2 is the approved-for-this-design-turn matching orthographic design sheet. This is a clean technical ART concept of separately modeled organic parts, not surgical gore.
Create a wide landscape technical production board on light warm-gray background with crisp dark small lettering, restrained amber/teal guide lines, realistic pearly tissue and blue-gray branching veins. Title text: "M-09  |  TISSUE ASSEMBLY". Preserve the exact same hanging legless creature, huge arms above its torso, wrist cuffs, shoulder metal rings, two small arms on the front and tapered multiple-eye crown below. No beam or room.
Layout:
LEFT 42 percent: full-body BACK view of the creature in the SAME hanging pose, showing a clear EXPLODED assembly. Torso with its two enormous upward arms remains centered; six membranes are displaced sideways from their real root attachments, exactly three on each side. At the viewer-left (creature's anatomical left in BACK view), put L1 upper/short outer, L2 middle, L3 lower/long inner. At viewer-right put R1, R2, R3 in matching positions. Label each individually next to the corresponding continuous membrane, with thin straight dashed leader to its attachment point on the back. Each leaf is a single thick-edged continuous veined skin lobe, scalloped edge and a few natural holes, never feather bunches or disconnected shredded strips. Exposed central torso is continuous flesh, no cut wounds. A slim golden ROOT BAND follows the two posterior shoulder/back root strips and stays on the body.
MIDDLE 30 percent: a neatly spaced six-part specimen grid, two columns three rows, one intact isolated membrane per cell, exactly these labels "L1" "R1" / "L2" "R2" / "L3" "R3". Parts same shape/material as exploded view. Small L1/R1, medium L2/R2, longest L3/R3. Each root has a small rounded fleshy attachment flange, thin structural vein runs from root to flexible tip. No metal fixtures on loose leaves. This grid defines ORGAN OBJECTS, not micro-ribbons; scallops remain part of their leaf.
RIGHT 28 percent: top small realistic BACK assembly detail with all six membranes closed, label "REST"; beneath, same back detail with six leaves fanned slightly outward from their real roots, label "PULSE". Neither miniature has new arms, extra wings or bird feathers; only membrane deployment changes. Bottom, one enlarged continuous leaf diagram overlaid with 3 joint circles on its long fleshy vein, "ROOT" then "MID" then "TIP"; ROOT band shaded amber, free middle/tip subtly teal. Root stays attached, mid and tip bend together in one smooth plane, no longitudinal corkscrew. A minimal arrow indicates controlled opening and another tiny arrow at tip indicates subtle secondary motion.
Tiny footer text only: "6 CONTINUOUS LOBES  /  FIXED ROOTS  /  BONE DRIVEN". Do not add paragraphs, measurements, numeric bone angles, heavy scaffolding or decorative story elements. The organ separation must remain unambiguous and the six root-to-tip continuous surfaces legible. Retain reference silhouette, organic asymmetry inside left/right structural pairing, and physical membrane thickness.

calls.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: image 1, the M09 Tissue Assembly technical board. Supporting image 2: the matching orthographic FRONT LEFT SIDE BACK turnaround. Preserve board layout, typography, all six detached membrane specimens, six labels L1/L2/L3/R1/R2/R3, amber root band and all right column diagrams exactly.
Make ONLY an anatomical orientation correction to the exposed body in the LARGE LEFT exploded figure which is explicitly labeled "(BACK)": replace the visible two crossed small arms on its lower front abdomen with the smooth continuous ridged BACK surface visible in the rightmost BACK view of image 2. Small arms exist only on the front side and MUST NOT be visible here. Keep the two giant upward suspension arms, metal shoulder rings, cuffs and eye-crown. The pendant eye-crown on the exploded back should match the smaller rear eyes and dorsal tissue folds in the BACK view of image 2, not the large frontal eyes. On this large central body REMOVE all remaining side membrane scraps still hanging behind/beside its torso because its exactly SIX detached leaves are already shown exploded outside; keep only the narrow integrated fleshy root strips on the back. Body remains legless with uninterrupted closed skin surface, no cut wounds.
Both miniature REST and PULSE images in the right column are also BACK views: keep their membrane arrangements and show no small crossed arms. Preserve original colors, rendering quality, soft neutral lighting, dimensions and frame. Do not add limbs, labels, organs, gore, arrows, specimens or extra panels.
